notes:
Top-level: building a VS Code copilot extension targeted at mid-market dev orgs. Primary ask: low-latency streaming completions and inline suggestions with pinning to well-tested model versions.

Key technical requirements (shorthand):
- p99 edit suggestion latency < 35ms ideally (local dev feel), p50 < 12ms for inline suggestions.
- Throughput baseline: 100 req/s peak per region for autocomplete streams (concurrency across teams).
- Streaming: token-by-token SSE or WebSocket to render incremental completions in editor. Must support partial tokens and cancellations.
- Model/version pinning: need stable model IDs for release channels (alpha/beta/prod); rollout/A-B needed.
- Caching: prefix caching encouraged for repeated code patterns; want Redwood Optimize recommendations.
- Auth/rate limits: will use SSO (SAML) + org-level billing. Concern: how rate limits applied for embedded extension (per-user vs per-org bucket). Asking for recommended client-side token-bucket strategy.
- Security: SOC2 required, audit logs for token usage, KMS support for key management, and EU data residency for paying customers.

Commercial notes: cost sensitive; early POC budget limited. Interested in dedicated pool if unit costs proven. Quoted ARR range \"50k-150k\".

Quotes / paraphrases from stakeholders:
- \"We need the inline suggestions to feel instantaneous — anything over 50ms is noticeable.\" — Head of Product
- \"If we can't pin models, shipping stable assistant behavior will be impossible.\" — Engineering Manager

POC goals (agreed):
- 2-week alpha integrated into internal VS Code build, measure p99 latency, token cost per suggestion, UX cancellation behavior.
- Validate streaming delivery (SSE + fallback), confirm rate limit behaviour under concurrent edits.

- Security to clear SSO/SAML flow and provide metadata endpoint.
- Confirm pricing for streaming tokens vs batch generation.
